section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study examining body appreciation (measured by the BAS) among Black college women in the United States. The study found that body appreciation had a moderate negative relation with BMI and was associated with reduced eating disorder risk factors, ethnic identity, and lower internalization of Western beauty ideals. The authors discuss the implications of their findings for understanding protective factors against eating disorders in Black women and note limitations including reliance on self-reported height and weight, use of a college sample, and lack of consideration for appearance factors particularly salient to Black women.
